name: stirling_cycle_ideal_regenerator
title: Ideal Stirling cycle with a perfect regenerator
summary: Theoretical Stirling cycle (two isotherms, two isochores) with an ideal regenerator: work and heat of the four transformations, net work, efficiency with and without regenerator compared with the Carnot efficiency. Every quantity is also computed with the real-gas air property functions, and the works of the two isotherms with the EES definite integral of p dv as well as in closed form.

verification.reference: EES stored solution of the source file (complete: all 68 variables hold a real value), compare_solution.py --ees-units, hand conversion from K/kPa/kJ to C/Pa/J; plus an independent re-implementation of the same exercise in Python/CoolProp (Simpson quadrature of the two integrals), not shipped; plus the Python/CoolProp solution of the same exercise shipped by the course for the previous year, which prints the same three efficiencies
verification.notes: On the runnable variant against the EES stored values: '66 common variables, 13 differ (rtol=0.001); only in EES: 2; only in CoolSolve: 5'. The 13 differences are s[1..4] and u[1..4] (constant reference-state offsets of the entropy/internal energy, CS-GAP-IDEAL-ENTROPY family; the isothermal entropy steps and the internal-energy differences agree) and the two isothermal works w_12_bis/w_34_bis with the heats and the efficiency derived from them (2.9e-02 to 4.3e-02), which are the quadrature error of EES: its step of 0.1 m^3/kg over 0.77 m^3/kg gives -204923 and 880721 J/kg when recomputed with CoolProp properties (against 202654 and 883256 stored), while the accurate value is -196811 and 845195 J/kg, i.e. CoolSolve's 196824 and -845201. Excluding exactly those 13 variables: '53 common variables, 0 differ (rtol=0.001)', largest deviation of the whole comparison 1.51e-05 (EES R# = 8314.3 vs 8314.4626 J/kmol-K). Against the Python/CoolProp re-implementation: '49 common variables, 5 differ (rtol=1e-6)', the five being the two integrals and their derived heats (max 5.04e-05, quadrature). Only in EES: p and v, stale workspace records; only in CoolSolve: fluid$ (CS-BUG-SOL-STRING), R#, the two integrals split out by the variant and its integration variable x.
